name: Parachurch
overview: Scripture reveals that the life of the believer is deeply rooted in community and shared purpose, as seen when Jesus promises His presence where believers gather in His name (Matthew 18:20) and the early church devoted themselves to apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer (Acts 2:42). The believers exemplified unity and selflessness, holding all things in common (Acts 4:32), and addressed practical needs within the body to maintain harmony and care (Acts 6:1). The churches experienced growth and spiritual edification through mutual encouragement and reverence for the Lord (Acts 9:31), reflecting the diverse yet unified functioning of the body of Christ, where each member has a distinct role (Romans 12:4). These passages collectively highlight the biblical foundation for parachurch ministries as extensions of the church's mission to support, equip, and serve the body of Christ in faithful community.
